@@ -3,7 +3,7 @@ title: Client ID Metadata Documents in Microsoft Entra ID

-ms.date: 09/21/2026

 ai-usage: ai-assisted
 
 #customer-intent: As an identity architect or developer, I want to understand how Microsoft Entra ID supports Client ID Metadata Documents so that I can decide whether CIMD is appropriate for my MCP client scenario.
@@ -11,16 +11,22 @@ ai-usage: ai-assisted
 
 # Client ID Metadata Documents in Microsoft Entra ID (preview)
 
-Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) let an OAuth client identify itself by using an HTTPS URL instead of a preassigned client ID. The document at that URL contains the client's OAuth metadata. Microsoft Entra ID retrieves and validates the document, represents the client as an agent identity in the tenant, and issues tokens under the tenant's existing consent and security policies.
+Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) are a new way to register OAuth clients with Entra ID. CIMD is primarily used by AI agents that need to connect to remote MCP servers.
 
 > [!IMPORTANT]
 > Client ID Metadata Document support in Microsoft Entra ID is in public preview. This preview is provided without a service-level agreement and isn't recommended for production workloads. Some features might be unsupported or have constrained capabilities. For more information, see [Universal License Terms for Online Services](https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/terms/product/ForOnlineServices/all).
 
-CIMD is useful when a client must connect to many authorization servers with which it has no prior relationship. For example, an MCP client can discover remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers at runtime, and each server might use a different authorization server. Requiring every client to be registered with every authorization server doesn't scale.
+## Why CIMD
 
-CIMD is defined by the [OAuth Client ID Metadata Document specification](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document/). The MCP authorization specification recommends CIMD for clients that don't have another supported registration mechanism.
+AI agents may use many different MCP servers to perform work. Some of these MCP servers may be secured by Entra's OAuth server — e.g. WorkIQ, Azure Storage MCP, or enterprise-built MCP servers. Others may be secured by a different OAuth server — e.g. GitHub, Workday, Slack. For general purpose AI agents, it's impractical to know all MCP servers it will use, and therefore impractical to know all OAuth servers the AI agent will encounter. The AI agent needs a way to dynamically register itself with an OAuth server and obtain a client ID.
 
-## How CIMD works with Microsoft Entra ID
+Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) let an OAuth client identify itself by using an HTTPS URL as its OAuth `client_id` value instead of a pre-registered client ID. A JSON document at that public URL contains the client's OAuth metadata, such as its redirect URIs and client credentials. This allows an OAuth server, such as Entra ID, to fetch the JSON document and use it to securely issue access tokens to the client.
+
+CIMD is useful when a client must connect to many authorization servers with which it has no prior relationship. For example, an AI agent can discover remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers at runtime, and each server might use a different authorization server. Requiring every client to be registered with every authorization server doesn't scale.
+
+CIMD is defined by the [OAuth Client ID Metadata Document specification](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document/).
+
+## How CIMD works
 
 A typical CIMD authorization flow has the following steps:
 
@@ -63,6 +69,37 @@ Implementers should always prefer pre-registration of a client with Entra when p
 
 An MCP client that discovers many remote servers at runtime is the primary scenario.
 
+## CIMD-enabled clients
+
+The following table lists clients that have been tested and validated against Entra's CIMD support.
+
+| Client | Client ID Metadata Document | Preview compatibility |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Claude Code | https://claude.ai/oauth/claude-code-client-metadata | Supported. |
+| Claude | https://claude.ai/oauth/mcp-oauth-client-metadata | Supported. |
+| Codex | https://chatgpt.com/oauth/codex/client.json | Supported. |
+| ChatGPT | https://chatgpt.com/oauth/client.json | Not supported. Its confidential-client authentication flow isn't supported by the Microsoft Entra preview. |
+| Visual Studio Code | https://vscode.dev/oauth/client-metadata.json | Not supported. Microsoft first-party clients do not use CIMD. |
+| GitHub Copilot | https://github.com/copilot/desktop/client-metadata.json | Not supported. Microsoft first-party clients do not use CIMD. |
+| Custom client built with the official MCP SDKs | Host a metadata document at a stable HTTPS URL on a domain you control. | Supported. |
+| Custom client implementation | Host a metadata document at a stable HTTPS URL on a domain you control. | Supported. |
+
+## CIMD-enabled MCP servers
+
+The following table is a non-exhaustive list of Microsoft MCP servers that have confirmed CIMD support.
+
+| MCP server | Remote MCP server URL | CIMD testing status |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Custom enterprise-built MCP server | -- | Supported, see [guide here](/entra/agent-id/secure-mcp-server-with-entra-id). |
+| [Microsoft MCP for IT Admins](https://github.com/microsoft/EnterpriseMCP) | `https://mcp.svc.cloud.microsoft/admin` | Not supported yet. |
+| [Azure Management MCP (ARM)](/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/azure-resource-manager-mcp-quickstart) | `https://mcp.management.azure.com` | Not supported yet. |
+| [Azure DevOps MCP](/azure/devops/mcp-server/remote-mcp-server) | `https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{organization}` | Not supported yet. |
+| [Work IQ MCP](/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/quickstart/github-copilot-cli) | `https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp` | Not supported yet. |
+| [Fabric IQ MCP](/fabric/iq/connectors/fabric-iq-mcp) | `https://fabriciq.svc.cloud.microsoft/v1/mcp/fabriciq` | Not supported yet. |
+| [Foundry MCP](/azure/foundry/mcp/get-started) | `https://mcp.ai.azure.com` | Not supported yet. |
+| [Microsoft Sentinel MCP](/azure/sentinel/datalake/sentinel-mcp-tools-overview) | `https://sentinel.microsoft.com/mcp/data-exploration` | Not supported yet. |
+| [Dataverse MCP](/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp) | `https://{dataverseOrgName}.crm.dynamics.com/api/mcp` | Not supported yet. |
+
 ## Supported capabilities and limitations
 
 The following table summarizes the capabilities and limitations of CIMD-backed agent identities.
@@ -77,6 +114,8 @@ The following table summarizes the capabilities and limitations of CIMD-backed a
 | Acting as an OAuth resource or token audience | Not supported |
 | ID tokens or SAML tokens for user sign-in | Not supported |
 | Shared client secrets | Not supported |
+| Confidential-client authentication, including `private_key_jwt` | Not supported during preview; keys in the metadata document aren't processed |
+| Microsoft first-party clients using CIMD | Not supported; use the existing first-party registration process |
 | Publisher verification or Microsoft 365 certification | Not supported |

@@ -96,7 +135,26 @@ Microsoft Entra ID applies the following protections:
 - **No app-only tokens:** CIMD clients can't use the client credentials grant.
 - **Audience restriction:** Microsoft Entra ID doesn't issue tokens whose audience is the CIMD client.
 
-Under the default recommended consent policy, users can consent only to low-risk OAuth permissions for CIMD clients. Sensitive permissions require administrator consent. For administrator guidance, see [Manage CIMD clients in Microsoft Entra ID](manage-client-id-metadata-document-clients.md).
+## Consent and permissions for clients using CIMD
+
+Entra treats clients using CIMD as unverified, and honors existing tenant consent policy. This means that the following rules apply:
+
+| Tenant Setting | What users can consent to |
+| -------------- | ------------------------- |
+| Default consent policy | Users can sign-in to CIMD clients. This creates an agent identity in the tenant. Users can only grant a very limited set of OAuth scopes to CIMD clients, such as `openid` and `User.Read` in Microsoft Graph. [Risk-based step up](/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-risk-based-step-up-consent) prevents users from granting any other permissions to CIMD clients. |
+| Do not allow user consent | In tenants that have disabled user consent via the **Do not allow user consent** setting in Entra Admin Center, users cannot consent to CIMD clients. This means they cannot add CIMD clients to their tenant, nor can they grant OAuth scopes to CIMD clients. |
+| Other consent policy | Using [consent policy](/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/manage-app-consent-policies), tenants can allow users to consent to CIMD clients. Administrators have fine-grained control over the conditions when user consent is allowed. |
+
+## Admin controls for CIMD
+
+Tenants can prevent users from adding CIMD clients or granting them new permissions via [consent policy](/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/manage-app-consent-policies). Use either of these approaches:
+
+- Block all user consent, via the **Do not allow user consent** setting in Entra Admin Center.
+- Allow user consent only for apps from verified publishers.
+
+Either of these policies will prevent non-admin users from adding CIMD clients to a tenant. Follow [Manage app consent policies](/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/manage-app-consent-policies) to configure consent policy in your tenant.
+
+To enable the use of a specific agent or client using CIMD, administrators can individually add agent identities to their tenant by providing the CIMD URL. This can be done via Entra Admin Center or Microsoft Graph APIs. See [Managing CIMD clients](./manage-client-id-metadata-document-clients.md).
 
 ## Governance considerations
 
@@ -109,7 +167,7 @@ Before using CIMD, account for the following considerations:
 - Entra doesn't provide a tenant-managed domain allowlist or blocklist for CIMD URLs.
 - Losing control of the document URL or its domain can affect every tenant that trusts that client identity.
 
-Use least-privilege delegated permissions, preapprove clients that need sensitive access, monitor their sign-ins, and remove identities that are no longer required.
+Always use least-privilege delegated permissions, preapprove clients that need sensitive access, monitor their sign-ins, and remove identities that are no longer required.

modifiedFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/manage-access-review.md b/docs/id-governance/manage-access-review.md index 2689247c955..2c5d2449503 100644 --- a/docs/id-governance/manage-access-review.md +++ b/docs/id-governance/manage-access-review.md @@ -8,138 +8,137 @@ ms.date: 03/12/2026 ms.reviewer: mwahl #Customer Intent: As an IT admin, I want to manage access reviews so that I can control user and guest access to groups and applications. --- - + # Manage user and guest user access with access reviews - + With access reviews, you can easily ensure that users or guests have appropriate access. You can ask the users themselves or a decision maker to participate in an access review and recertify (or attest) to users' access. The reviewers can give their input on each user's need for continued access based on suggestions from Microsoft Entra ID. When an access review is finished, you can then make changes and remove access from users who no longer need it. - + > [!NOTE] > This article discusses conducting access reviews for users and applications. To see information on conducting an access review for multiple resources in access packages see here [Review access of an access package in Microsoft Entra entitlement management](entitlement-management-access-reviews-review-access.md). If you want to review user or service principal access to Microsoft Entra ID or Azure resource roles, see [Start an access review in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management](../id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-create-roles-and-resource-roles-review.md). - + ## Prerequisites - + [!INCLUDE [Microsoft Entra ID Governance license](../includes/entra-entra-governance-license.md)] - + ## Create and perform an access review for users First, you must be assigned as at least one of the following roles: - User Administrator -- Identity Governance Administrator +- Identity Governance Administrator - Privileged Role Administrator (for reviews of role-assignable groups only) -- (Preview) Microsoft 365 or Microsoft Entra Security Group owner of the group to be reviewed +- (Preview) Microsoft 365 or Microsoft Entra Security Group owner of the group to be reviewed Then, go to the [Identity Governance page](https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_AAD_ERM/DashboardBlade/) to ensure that access reviews are ready for your organization. -You can have one or more users as reviewers in an access review. - -1. Select a group in Microsoft Entra ID that has one or more members. Or select an application connected to Microsoft Entra ID that has one or more users assigned to it. - +You can have one or more users as reviewers in an access review. + +1. Select a group in Microsoft Entra ID that has one or more members. Or select an application connected to Microsoft Entra ID that has one or more users assigned to it. + 2. Decide whether to have each user review their own access or to have one or more users review everyone's access. - + 3. In one of the previously listed roles, go to the [Identity Governance page](https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_AAD_ERM/DashboardBlade/). - + 4. Create the access review. For more information, see [Create an access review of groups or applications](create-access-review.md). - + 5. When the access review starts, ask the reviewers to give input. By default, they each receive an email from Microsoft Entra ID with a link to the access panel, where they [review access to groups or applications](self-access-review.md). - + 6. If the reviewers haven't given input, you can ask Microsoft Entra ID to send them a reminder. By default, Microsoft Entra ID automatically sends a reminder halfway to the end date to all reviewers. - + 7. After the reviewers give input, stop the access review and apply the changes. For more information, see [Complete an access review of groups or applications](complete-access-review.md). - + ## Manage guest access with Microsoft Entra access reviews - + With Microsoft Entra ID, you can easily enable collaboration across organizational boundaries by using the [Microsoft Entra B2B feature](../external-id/what-is-b2b.md). Guest users from other tenants can be [invited by administrators](../external-id/add-users-administrator.yml) or by [other users](../external-id/what-is-b2b.md). This capability also applies to social identities such as Microsoft accounts. - - - + + + ## Create and perform an access review for guests - + The same roles required to create an access review for users are also required to create an access review for guests. For more information, see [Create and perform an access review for users](manage-access-review.md#create-and-perform-an-access-review-for-users). Microsoft Entra ID enables several scenarios for reviewing guest users. - + You can review either: - + - A group in Microsoft Entra ID that has one or more guests as members. - - An application connected to Microsoft Entra ID that has one or more guest users assigned to it. - -When reviewing guest user access to Microsoft 365 groups, you can either create a review for each group individually or turn on automatic, recurring access reviews of guest users across all Microsoft 365 groups. The following video provides more information on recurring access reviews of guest users: - + - An application connected to Microsoft Entra ID that has one or more guest users assigned to it. + +When reviewing guest user access to Microsoft 365 groups, you can either create a review for each group individually or turn on automatic, recurring access reviews of guest users across all Microsoft 365 groups. The following video provides more information on recurring access reviews of guest users: + > [!VIDEO https://www.youtube.com/embed/3D2_YW2DwQ8] - + You can then decide whether to ask each guest to review their own access or to ask one or more users to review every guest's access. - + These scenarios are covered in the following sections. - + ### Ask guests to review their own membership in a group - + You can use access reviews to ensure that users who were invited and added to a group continue to need access. You can easily ask guests to review their own membership in that group. - + 1. To create an access review for the group, select the review to include guest user members only and that members review themselves. For more information, see [Create an access review of groups or applications](create-access-review.md). - + 2. Ask each guest to review their own membership. By default, each guest who accepted an invitation receives an email from Microsoft Entra ID with a link to the access review. Microsoft Entra ID has instructions for guests on how to [review access to groups or applications](self-access-review.md). - + 3. After the reviewers give input, stop the access review and apply the changes. For more information, see [Complete an access review of groups or applications](complete-access-review.md). - + 4. In addition to those users who denied their own need for continued access, you can also remove users who didn't respond. - + 5. If the group isn't used for access management, you also can remove users who weren't selected to participate in the review because they didn't accept their invitation. Not accepting might indicate that the invited user's email address had a typo. If a group is used as a distribution list, perhaps some guest users weren't selected to participate because they're contact objects. - + ### Ask a sponsor to review a guest's membership in a group - + You can ask a sponsor, such as the owner of a group, to review a guest's need for continued membership in a group. - + 1. To create an access review for the group, select the review to include guest user members only. Then specify one or more reviewers. For more information, see [Create an access review of groups or applications](create-access-review.md). - + 2. Ask the reviewers to give input. By default, they each receive an email from Microsoft Entra ID with a link to the access panel, where they [review access to groups or applications](self-access-review.md). - + 3. After the reviewers give input, stop the access review and apply the changes. For more information, see [Complete an access review of groups or applications](complete-access-review.md). > [!NOTE] -> You can block external identities from signing-in to your tenant and delete the external identities from your tenant after 30 days. During this period, settings, results, reviewers or Audit logs under the current review won't be viewable or configurable. For more information, see [Disable and delete external identities with Microsoft Entra access reviews -](access-reviews-external-users.md#disable-and-delete-external-identities-with-azure-ad-access-reviews). +> You can block external identities from signing-in to your tenant and delete the external identities from your tenant after 30 days. During this period, settings, results, reviewers or Audit logs under the current review won't be viewable or configurable. For more information, see [Disable and delete external identities with Microsoft Entra access reviews](access-reviews-external-users.md#disable-and-delete-external-identities-with-azure-ad-access-reviews). + - ### Ask guests to review their own access to an application - + You can use access reviews to ensure that users who were invited for a particular application continue to need access. You can easily ask the guests themselves to review their own need for access. - + 1. To create an access review for the application, select the review to include guests only and that users review their own access. For more information, see [Create an access review of groups or applications](create-access-review.md). - + 2. Ask each guest to review their own access to the application. By default, each guest who accepted an invitation receives an email from Microsoft Entra ID. That email has a link to the access review in your organization's access panel. Microsoft Entra ID has instructions for guests on how to [review access to groups or applications](self-access-review.md). - + 3. After the reviewers give input, stop the access review and apply the changes. For more information, see [Complete an access review of groups or applications](complete-access-review.md). - -4. In addition to users who denied their own need for continued access, you also can remove guest users who didn't respond or who weren't selected to participate, especially if they weren't recently invited. Those users didn't accept their invitation and so didn't have access to the application. - + +4. In addition to users who denied their own need for continued access, you also can remove guest users who didn't respond or who weren't selected to participate, especially if they weren't recently invited. Those users didn't accept their invitation and so didn't have access to the application. + ### Ask a sponsor to review a guest's access to an application - + You can ask a sponsor, such as the owner of an application, to review a guest's need for continued access to the application. - + 1. To create an access review for the application, select the review to include guests only. Then specify one or more users as reviewers. For more information, see [Create an access review of groups or applications](create-access-review.md). - + 2. Ask the reviewers to give input. By default, they each receive an email from Microsoft Entra ID with a link to the access panel, where they [review access to groups or applications](self-access-review.md). - + 3. After the reviewers give input, stop the access review and apply the changes. For more information, see [Complete an access review of groups or applications](complete-access-review.md). - + ### Ask guests to review their need for access, in general - + In some organizations, guests might not be aware of their group memberships. - - + + 1. Create a security group in Microsoft Entra ID with the guests as members, if a suitable group doesn't already exist. For example, you can create a group with a manually maintained membership of guests. Or, you can create a dynamic group with a name such as "Guests of Contoso" for users in the Contoso tenant who have the UserType attribute value of Guest. Keep in mind that a guest user who is a member of the group can see the other members of the group. - + 2. To create an access review for that group, select the reviewers to be the members themselves. For more information, see [Create an access review of groups or applications](create-access-review.md). - -3. Ask each guest to review their own membership. By default, each guest who accepted an invitation receives an email from Microsoft Entra ID with a link to the access review in your organization's access panel. Microsoft Entra ID has instructions for guests on how to [review access to groups or applications](perform-access-review.md). - + +3. Ask each guest to review their own membership. By default, each guest who accepted an invitation receives an email from Microsoft Entra ID with a link to the access review in your organization's access panel. Microsoft Entra ID has instructions for guests on how to [review access to groups or applications](perform-access-review.md). + 4. After the reviewers give input, stop the access review. For more information, see [Complete an access review of groups or applications](complete-access-review.md). - + 5. Remove guest access for guests who were denied, didn't complete the review, or didn't previously accept their invitation. If some of the guests are contacts who were selected to participate in the review or they didn't previously accept an invitation, you can disable their accounts by using the Microsoft Entra admin center or PowerShell. If the guest no longer needs access and isn't a contact, you can remove their user object from your directory by using the Microsoft Entra admin center or PowerShell to delete the guest user object. - + ## Next steps - + [Create an access review of groups or applications](create-access-review.md)

englishSummary.headline: Microsoft Entra Connect Health alert catalog updated

messageCenterItems.title: Copilot Studio - Create Dataverse agent users with Microsoft Entra agent 's user account
messageCenterItems.summary: We are announcing the ability to create Dataverse agent users with Microsoft Entra agent's user account in Copilot Studio.  This feature will reach general availability on December 8th, 2026.
messageCenterItems.body:
We are announcing the ability to create Dataverse agent users with Microsoft Entra agent's user account in Copilot Studio. This feature will reach general availability on December 8th, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature enables you to securely deploy agents to access and interact with Dataverse data by using enterprise-managed Microsoft Entra agent identities. It enables agents to be provisioned as Dataverse agent users with dedicated, least-privileged security roles based on their intended capabilities.

The feature ensures agents have only the access required to perform tasks autonomously or on behalf of users. By using identity-based role assignment and full auditing of agent-driven actions, you can enforce security and compliance policies across both human users and agents while maintaining traceability of data access and changes within Dataverse environments.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Create Entra agent users (preview).
